   260	/-- **Fibrewise large-twist vanishing** (FLV-fiber, the Wave-4 headline; conditional form
   261	for a dominant affine `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`): for every Weil divisor `D` on the curve bundle `Y`,
   262	the degree-one cohomology of the twisted divisor sheaf `𝒪(D + n·F)`, `F` the fiber divisor
   263	of `π`, vanishes for all sufficiently large `n`. The bound `n₀` is per-class and
   264	non-effective — Noetherian stabilization of the exhausting fiber-lattice chain inside the
   265	finite-codimension ambient `N`, per `informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §2.1; no duality, no
   266	`R¹f_*`. The two `Module.Finite` hypotheses are the structure-sheaf properness inputs of
   267	the landed dévissage (`moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one`). -/
   268	theorem subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isDominant_toP1
   269	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
   270	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
   271	    (D : Y.CurveDivisor) :
   272	    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀,
   273	      Subsingleton
   274	        (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1) := by
   275	  haveI hfin : Module.Finite K
   276	      (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)
   277	        ⧸ fiberLatticeOverlap π D 0) :=
   278	    Module.Finite.equiv (fiberLatticeH1Equiv π D 0)
   279	  obtain ⟨n₀, hn₀⟩ := Submodule.eventually_eq_top_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top
   280	    (fiberLatticeOverlap_mono π D) (iSup_fiberLatticeOverlap π D)
   281	  refine ⟨n₀, fun n hn => ?_⟩
   282	  haveI : Subsingleton (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)
   283	      ⧸ fiberLatticeOverlap π D n) :=
   284	    Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr (hn₀ n hn)
   285	  exact (fiberLatticeH1Equiv π D n).toEquiv.subsingleton
   286	
   287	end Carrier

   290	
   291	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
   292	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   293	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   294	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   295	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   296	
   297	/-- **Fibrewise large-twist vanishing along a finite map** (the worksheet-shaped form,
   298	`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §1.2): for a **finite** dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` compatible
   299	with the structure morphisms, the base `H¹(𝒪_Y)`-finiteness input is discharged from
   300	finiteness of `π` (`moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`); only the `H⁰` properness
   301	input remains a hypothesis. -/
   302	theorem subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1
   303	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
   304	    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
   305	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (D : Y.CurveDivisor) :
   306	    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀,
   307	      Subsingleton
   308	        (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1) :=
   309	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
   310	    moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ
   311	  subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isDominant_toP1 π D
   312	
   313	end Main

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMapToolkit

     8	/-!
     9	# Functoriality of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
    10	
    11	The Layer-2 functor `picEt` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEt`) is functorial along an
    12	*arbitrary* morphism `f : T' ⟶ T` of test objects: the value of the restricted family at
    13	an affine open `W ⊆ T'.left` — whose `f`-image need not lie in any affine open of
    14	`T.left` — is *glued* over a finite basic-open refinement of `W` subordinate to the
    15	preimages of affine opens, using the Zariski sheaf property of the affine étale Picard
    16	functor (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtAffZariskiSep`, `PicEtAffZariskiGlue`) whose
    17	gluing half is licensed by the (C1) étale separatedness.
    18	
    19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt.IsPullbackValue`: the characterizing property of the glued
    20	  value — on every affine sub-open lying in the preimage of an affine open, it restricts
    21	  to the pullback of the family value there.  Values with this property are unique
    22	  (`pullbackValue_unique`, from Zariski separation) and exist
    23	  (`exists_isPullbackValue`, from Zariski gluing).
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtMap C f : picEt C T →* picEt C T'` with the functor laws
    25	  `picEtMap_id` and `picEtMap_comp`, and the functor
    26	  `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtFunctor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv_naturality`: the affine comparison
    28	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEt`) is natural in the test algebra.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt.ext_of_le_cover`: **uniqueness of gluings** — two sections of
    30	  `picEt C T` agreeing on every affine open subordinate to an open cover of `T.left`
    31	  are equal (the separation half of the sheaf property of `picEt` itself).
    32	-/
    33	
    34	set_option autoImplicit false
    35	
    36	universe u
    37	
    38	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace
    39	
    40	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    41	
    42	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
    43	
    44	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    45	
    46	namespace picEt
    47	
    48	variable {T T' T'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    49	
    50	/-! ## The characterizing property of the glued value -/
    51	
    52	/-- The characterizing property of the value at `W` of the restriction of `s` along
    53	`f`: on every affine sub-open of `W` contained in the preimage of an affine open `V` of
    54	the target, it restricts to the pullback of the value of `s` at `V`. -/
    55	def IsPullbackValue (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : picEt C T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens)
    56	    (v : PicEtAff C Γ(T'.left, W.1)) : Prop :=
    57	  ∀ (W₀ : T'.left.affineOpens) (hW₀ : W₀.1 ≤ W.1) (V : T.left.affineOpens)
    58	    (hV : W₀.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
    59	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T' hW₀) v
    60	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W₀.1 hV) (s.1 V)
    61	
    62	/-- Values with the pullback property are unique. -/
    63	theorem pullbackValue_unique {f : T' ⟶ T} {s : picEt C T} {W : T'.left.affineOpens}
    64	    {v v' : PicEtAff C Γ(T'.left, W.1)} (hv : IsPullbackValue C f s W v)
    65	    (hv' : IsPullbackValue C f s W v') : v = v' := by
    66	  classical
    67	  obtain ⟨sub, hspan, hsub⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W.2
    68	    (fun U₀ => ∃ V : T.left.affineOpens, U₀ = f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)
    69	    (fun w _ => by
    70	      obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hfwV, -⟩ := Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
    71	        T.left.isBasis_affineOpens (show f.left.base w ∈ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) from trivial)
    72	      exact ⟨f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V, hfwV, ⟨⟨V, hVaff⟩, rfl⟩⟩)
    73	  refine eq_of_basic_eq C W sub hspan (fun r hr => ?_)
    74	  obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨V, rfl⟩, hle⟩ := hsub r hr
    75	  rw [hv ⟨_, W.2.basicOpen r⟩ (T'.left.basicOpen_le r) V hle,
    76	    hv' ⟨_, W.2.basicOpen r⟩ (T'.left.basicOpen_le r) V hle]
    77

    80	/-- The conversion between the abstract localization map of a basic-open inclusion and
    81	the section restriction. -/
    82	private lemma algHomOfDvd_eq_resAlgHom (W : T'.left.affineOpens)
    83	    (a b : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) (hle : T'.left.basicOpen b ≤ T'.left.basicOpen a)
    84	    (hdvd : a ∣ b) :
    85	    haveI := W.2.isLocalization_basicOpen a
    86	    haveI := W.2.isLocalization_basicOpen b
    87	    (IsLocalization.Away.algHomOfDvd a b Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen a)
    88	      Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen b) hdvd).restrictScalars k
    89	      = Over.resAlgHom T' hle := by
    90	  haveI := W.2.isLocalization_basicOpen a
    91	  haveI := W.2.isLocalization_basicOpen b
    92	  haveI hsub : Subsingleton (Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen a)
    93	      →ₐ[Γ(T'.left, W.1)] Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen b)) :=
    94	    IsLocalization.algHom_subsingleton (Submonoid.powers a)
    95	  rw [show IsLocalization.Away.algHomOfDvd a b Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen a)
    96	      Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen b) hdvd = Over.resAwayAlgHom T' hle from
    97	    Subsingleton.elim _ _]
    98	  exact Over.resAwayAlgHom_restrictScalars T' hle

   100	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   101	-- The instance towers over the section rings of the basic refinement exceed the
   102	-- default elaboration budget.
   103	/-- **Existence of the glued value**: the restriction of a compatible family along an
   104	arbitrary morphism of test objects has a value at every affine open of the source,
   105	glued over a finite basic-open refinement subordinate to the preimages of affine
   106	opens. -/
   107	theorem exists_isPullbackValue (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : picEt C T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) :
   108	    ∃ v, IsPullbackValue C f s W v := by
   109	  classical
   110	  -- the basic refinement subordinate to preimages of affine opens
   111	  obtain ⟨sub, hspan, hsub⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W.2
   112	    (fun U₀ => ∃ V : T.left.affineOpens, U₀ = f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)
   113	    (fun w _ => by
   114	      obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hfwV, -⟩ := Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
   115	        T.left.isBasis_affineOpens (show f.left.base w ∈ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) from trivial)
   116	      exact ⟨f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V, hfwV, ⟨⟨V, hVaff⟩, rfl⟩⟩)
   117	  have hsub' : ∀ r ∈ sub, ∃ V : T.left.affineOpens,
   118	      T'.left.basicOpen r ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 := fun r hr => by
   119	    obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨V, rfl⟩, hle⟩ := hsub r hr
   120	    exact ⟨V, hle⟩
   121	  choose Vc hVc using hsub'
   122	  -- the local values
   123	  haveI hAway : ∀ r : ↥sub, IsLocalization.Away (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))
   124	      Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))) := fun r =>
   125	    W.2.isLocalization_basicOpen (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))
   126	  haveI hAwayT : ∀ r r' : ↥sub,
   127	      IsLocalization.Away ((r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) * (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))
   128	        Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen
   129	          ((r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) * (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))) := fun r r' =>
   130	    W.2.isLocalization_basicOpen _
   131	  have hbmul : ∀ r r' : ↥sub,
   132	      T'.left.basicOpen ((r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) * (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))
   133	        ≤ T'.left.basicOpen (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) := fun r r' => by
   134	    rw [Scheme.basicOpen_mul]
   135	    exact inf_le_left
   136	  have hbmul' : ∀ r r' : ↥sub,
   137	      T'.left.basicOpen ((r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) * (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))
   138	        ≤ T'.left.basicOpen (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) := fun r r' => by
   139	    rw [Scheme.basicOpen_mul]
   140	    exact inf_le_right
   141	  -- glue
   142	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := PicEtAff.exists_mapAlg_eq_of_compat C
   143	    (fun r : ↥sub => (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))
   144	    (fun r : ↥sub => Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1))))
   145	    (fun r r' : ↥sub => Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen
   146	      ((r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)) * (r' : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))))
   147	    (by
   148	      have hr : (Set.range fun r : ↥sub => (r : Γ(T'.left, W.1)))
   149	          = (↑sub : Set Γ(T'.left, W.1)) := Subtype.range_coe
   150	      rw [hr]
   151	      exact hspan)
   152	    (fun r => PicEtAff.mapAlg C
   153	      (Over.appLEAlgHom f (Vc r.1 r.2).1 (T'.left.basicOpen r.1) (hVc r.1 r.2)) (s.1 (Vc r.1 r.2)))
   154	    (fun r r' => by
   155	      -- the overlap compatibility, from choice independence
   156	      rw [algHomOfDvd_eq_resAlgHom W r.1 (r.1 * r'.1) (hbmul r r') (dvd_mul_right _ _),
   157	        algHomOfDvd_eq_resAlgHom W r'.1 (r.1 * r'.1) (hbmul' r r') (dvd_mul_left _ _),
   158	        ← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp, ← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp,
   159	        Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom, Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom]
   160	      exact mapAlg_appLE_eq C f s
   161	        (W₀ := ⟨_, W.2.basicOpen (r.1 * r'.1)⟩) _ _)
   162	  -- the glued value has the pullback property
   163	  refine ⟨z, fun W₀ hW₀ V hV => ?_⟩
   164	  obtain ⟨sub₀, hspan₀, hsub₀⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W₀.2
   165	    (fun U₀ => ∃ r ∈ sub, U₀ = T'.left.basicOpen r)
   166	    (fun w hw => by
   167	      have hwW : w ∈ (⨆ r ∈ (↑sub : Set Γ(T'.left, W.1)), T'.left.basicOpen r) := by
   168	        rw [iSup_basicOpen_of_span_eq_top _ _ hspan]
   169	        exact hW₀ hw
   170	      obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp hwW
   171	      obtain ⟨hrsub, hwr⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp hr
   172	      exact ⟨T'.left.basicOpen r, hwr, ⟨r, hrsub, rfl⟩⟩)
   173	  refine eq_of_basic_eq C W₀ sub₀ hspan₀ (fun q hq => ?_)
   174	  obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨r, hr, rfl⟩, hqle⟩ := hsub₀ q hq
   175	  -- the left side restricts through the glued datum
   176	  have hL : PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le q))
   177	      (PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T' hW₀) z)
   178	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.appLEAlgHom f (Vc r hr).1 (T'.left.basicOpen q)
   179	          (hqle.trans (hVc r hr))) (s.1 (Vc r hr)) := by
   180	    have hzr := hz ⟨r, hr⟩
   181	    rw [show IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k Γ(T'.left, W.1)
   182	        Γ(T'.left, T'.left.basicOpen r)
   183	      = Over.resAlgHom T' (T'.left.basicOpen_le r) from AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl] at hzr
   184	    rw [← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp,
   185	      show ((T'.left.basicOpen_le q).trans hW₀ :
   186	          T'.left.basicOpen q ≤ W.1)
   187	        = (hqle.trans (T'.left.basicOpen_le r)) from rfl,
   188	      ← Over.resAlgHom_comp T' hqle (T'.left.basicOpen_le r), PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp,
   189	      hzr, ← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom]
   190	  -- the right side restricts directly
   191	  rw [hL, ← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp_appLEAlgHom]
   192	  exact mapAlg_appLE_eq C f s (W₀ := ⟨_, W₀.2.basicOpen q⟩) _ _
   193	
   194	/-- Existence and uniqueness of the glued value. -/
   195	theorem existsUnique_isPullbackValue (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : picEt C T)
   196	    (W : T'.left.affineOpens) : ∃! v, IsPullbackValue C f s W v := by
   197	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := exists_isPullbackValue C f s W
   198	  exact ⟨v, hv, fun v' hv' => pullbackValue_unique C hv' hv⟩
   199	
   200	end picEt

   206	variable {T T' T'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   207	variable [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]

   209	open picEt
   210	
   211	/-- The value of the restricted family at an affine open of the source. -/
   212	noncomputable def picEtMapVal (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : picEt C T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) :
   213	    PicEtAff C Γ(T'.left, W.1) :=
   214	  (existsUnique_isPullbackValue C f s W).choose
   215	
   216	lemma picEtMapVal_spec (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : picEt C T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) :
   217	    IsPullbackValue C f s W (picEtMapVal C f s W) :=
   218	  (existsUnique_isPullbackValue C f s W).choose_spec.1
   219	
   220	lemma picEtMapVal_eq_of (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : picEt C T) {W : T'.left.affineOpens}
   221	    {v : PicEtAff C Γ(T'.left, W.1)} (hv : IsPullbackValue C f s W v) :
   222	    picEtMapVal C f s W = v :=
   223	  pullbackValue_unique C (picEtMapVal_spec C f s W) hv
   224	
   225	/-- The value of the restricted family on an affine open lying in the preimage of an
   226	affine open is the plain pullback. -/
   227	lemma picEtMapVal_eq_mapAlg (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : picEt C T) {W : T'.left.affineOpens}
   228	    {V : T.left.affineOpens} (hV : W.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) :
   229	    picEtMapVal C f s W = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W.1 hV) (s.1 V) := by
   230	  have h := picEtMapVal_spec C f s W W le_rfl V hV
   231	  rwa [Over.resAlgHom_rfl, PicEtAff.mapAlg_id] at h
   232	
   233	/-- **Restriction of `picEt` along an arbitrary morphism of test objects.** -/
   234	noncomputable def picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) : picEt C T →* picEt C T' where
   235	  toFun s := ⟨fun W => picEtMapVal C f s W, by
   236	    intro U V h
   237	    refine (picEtMapVal_eq_of C f s (W := U) ?_).symm
   238	    intro W₀ hW₀ V' hV'
   239	    rw [← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp]
   240	    exact picEtMapVal_spec C f s V W₀ (hW₀.trans h) V' hV'⟩
   241	  map_one' := by
   242	    refine picEt.ext fun W => ?_
   243	    change picEtMapVal C f 1 W = 1
   244	    refine picEtMapVal_eq_of C f 1 ?_
   245	    intro W₀ hW₀ V hV
   246	    rw [picEt.one_val, map_one, map_one]
   247	  map_mul' s t := by
   248	    refine picEt.ext fun W => ?_
   249	    change picEtMapVal C f (s * t) W = picEtMapVal C f s W * picEtMapVal C f t W
   250	    refine picEtMapVal_eq_of C f (s * t) ?_
   251	    intro W₀ hW₀ V hV
   252	    rw [picEt.mul_val, map_mul, map_mul,
   253	      picEtMapVal_spec C f s W W₀ hW₀ V hV, picEtMapVal_spec C f t W W₀ hW₀ V hV]
   254	
   255	@[simp]
   256	lemma picEtMap_val (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : picEt C T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) :
   257	    (picEtMap C f s).1 W = picEtMapVal C f s W :=
   258	  rfl
   259	
   260	/-- The functor law: restriction along the identity is the identity. -/
   261	theorem picEtMap_id (s : picEt C T) : picEtMap C (𝟙 T) s = s := by
   262	  refine picEt.ext fun W => ?_
   263	  rw [picEtMap_val]
   264	  refine picEtMapVal_eq_of C (𝟙 T) s ?_
   265	  intro W₀ hW₀ V hV
   266	  have hV' : W₀.1 ≤ V.1 := by
   267	    intro p hp
   268	    have hmem := hV hp
   269	    rw [Over.id_left] at hmem
   270	    exact hmem
   271	  rw [Over.appLEAlgHom_id T V.1 W₀.1 hV hV', s.compat W₀ W hW₀, s.compat W₀ V hV']
   272	
   273	/-- The functor law: restriction along a composite is the composite of the
   274	restrictions. -/
   275	theorem picEtMap_comp (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T'' ⟶ T') (s : picEt C T) :
   276	    picEtMap C (g ≫ f) s = picEtMap C g (picEtMap C f s) := by
   277	  classical
   278	  refine picEt.ext fun W => ?_
   279	  rw [picEtMap_val, picEtMap_val]
   280	  refine (picEtMapVal_eq_of C (g ≫ f) s ?_)
   281	  intro W₀ hW₀ V hV
   282	  -- refine by basic opens whose `g`-image lies in an affine open inside `f⁻¹ V`
   283	  obtain ⟨sub, hspan, hsub⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover W₀.2
   284	    (fun U₀ => ∃ V'' : T'.left.affineOpens,
   285	      V''.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ U₀ = g.left ⁻¹ᵁ V''.1)
   286	    (fun w hw => by
   287	      have hgw : g.left.base w ∈ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 := by
   288	        have := hV hw
   289	        rw [Over.comp_left] at this
   290	        exact this
   291	      obtain ⟨V'', hV''aff, hgwV'', hV''le⟩ := Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp
   292	        T'.left.isBasis_affineOpens hgw
   293	      exact ⟨g.left ⁻¹ᵁ V'', hgwV'', ⟨⟨V'', hV''aff⟩, hV''le, rfl⟩⟩)
   294	  refine eq_of_basic_eq C W₀ sub hspan (fun q hq => ?_)
   295	  obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨V'', hV''le, rfl⟩, hqle⟩ := hsub q hq
   296	  -- the left side, through the two glued values
   297	  have hL : PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T'' (T''.left.basicOpen_le q))
   298	      (PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T'' hW₀)
   299	        (picEtMapVal C g (picEtMap C f s) W))
   300	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.appLEAlgHom g V''.1 (T''.left.basicOpen q) hqle)

     9	/-!
    10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor on all test objects: the object level
    11	
    12	For a curve `C` over `k`, the étale-sheafified relative Picard group of an **affine**
    13	test is the one-step plus construction `PicEtAff C A` (étale-separatedness of the
    14	relative Picard presheaf makes one plus suffice — axiom (C1),
    15	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechKernelLemma`).  The frozen group-object interface forces
    16	the functor to exist on **all** of `Over (Spec k)`; following the resolution of the
    17	Layer-2 vehicle question (inbox I-0140), the extension is the *bespoke affine-opens
    18	limit*: a section over a test object `T` is a compatible family of plus classes over the
    19	affine opens of `T.left`, valued in `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)` via the section-ring
    20	algebras of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtSections`.  The index poset is `Type u`-small,
    21	which is the point of the vehicle.
    22	
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt C T`: the limit, as the subgroup of the product over
    24	  `T.left.affineOpens` cut out by compatibility under restriction, with its `CommGroup`
    25	  structure; `picEt.eval` is evaluation at an affine open.
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.congr C e`: transport of plus classes along an isomorphism
    27	  of test algebras.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv C A`: **the affine comparison** — on an affine
    29	  test `overSpec k A`, evaluation at the top affine open is a group isomorphism
    30	  `picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃* PicEtAff C A` (the affine-opens poset of an affine test has
    31	  a terminal element, so the limit collapses).
    32	
    33	Functoriality in `T` — restriction along an arbitrary morphism of test objects, by
    34	gluing over basic-open refinements, licensed by (C1)-separatedness — is built on top of
    35	the Zariski sheaf property of `PicEtAff` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap`.
    36	-/
    37	
    38	set_option autoImplicit false
    39	
    40	universe u
    41	
    42	open CategoryTheory
    43	
    44	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    45	
    46	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    47	
    48	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
    49	
    50	noncomputable section
    51	
    52	/-! ## Transport of plus classes along an isomorphism of test algebras -/
    53	
    54	namespace PicEtAff
    55	
    56	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    57	
    58	/-- Transport of étale-plus Picard classes along an isomorphism of test algebras. -/
    59	def congr (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) : PicEtAff C A ≃* PicEtAff C B where
    60	  toFun := mapAlg C e.toAlgHom
    61	  invFun := mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom
    62	  left_inv x := by
    63	    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.symm.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k A from
    64	      AlgHom.ext fun a => e.symm_apply_apply a]
    65	    exact mapAlg_id C x
    66	  right_inv x := by
    67	    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.toAlgHom.comp e.symm.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k B from
    68	      AlgHom.ext fun b => e.apply_symm_apply b]
    69	    exact mapAlg_id C x
    70	  map_mul' x y := map_mul (mapAlg C e.toAlgHom) x y
    71	
    72	@[simp]
    73	lemma congr_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C A) :
    74	    congr C e x = mapAlg C e.toAlgHom x :=
    75	  rfl
    76	
    77	@[simp]
    78	lemma congr_symm_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C B) :
    79	    (congr C e).symm x = mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom x :=
    80	  rfl
    81	
    82	end PicEtAff

    84	/-! ## The affine-opens limit -/
    85	
    86	variable (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    87	
    88	/-- The compatible families over the affine opens of the test object, as a subgroup of
    89	the product of the affine-level plus groups: the value at a smaller affine open is the
    90	restriction of the value at a larger one. -/
    91	def picEtSubgroup :
    92	    Subgroup (Π U : T.left.affineOpens, PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1)) where
    93	  carrier := {s | ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
    94	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}
    95	  one_mem' := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one]
    96	  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb := fun U V h => by
    97	    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, ha U V h, hb U V h]
    98	  inv_mem' {a} ha := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, map_inv, ha U V h]
    99	
   100	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor at an arbitrary test object**, object
   101	level: compatible families of affine-level plus classes over the affine opens of
   102	`T.left` — the bespoke affine-opens limit of `PicEtAff C ∘ Γ(T.left, ·)`.  On affine
   103	tests this is `PicEtAff` itself (`picEtAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its
   104	canonical Zariski-continuous extension. -/
   105	def picEt : Type u :=
   106	  picEtSubgroup C T
   107	
   108	noncomputable instance : CommGroup (picEt C T) :=
   109	  inferInstanceAs (CommGroup (picEtSubgroup C T))
   110	
   111	namespace picEt
   112	
   113	variable {C T}
   114	
   115	/-- The compatibility of a section of `picEt` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/
   116	lemma compat (s : picEt C T) (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
   117	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
   118	  s.2 U V h
   119	
   120	@[ext]
   121	lemma ext {s t : picEt C T} (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, s.1 U = t.1 U) : s = t :=
   122	  Subtype.ext (funext h)
   123	
   124	variable (C T) in
   125	/-- Evaluation of a section of `picEt` at an affine open, as a group homomorphism. -/
   126	def eval (U : T.left.affineOpens) : picEt C T →* PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1) :=
   127	  (Pi.evalMonoidHom (fun V : T.left.affineOpens => PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, V.1)) U).comp
   128	    (picEtSubgroup C T).subtype
   129	
   130	@[simp]
   131	lemma eval_apply (U : T.left.affineOpens) (s : picEt C T) : eval C T U s = s.1 U :=
   132	  rfl
   133	
   134	@[simp]
   135	lemma mul_val (s t : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
   136	    (s * t).1 U = s.1 U * t.1 U :=
   137	  rfl
   138	
   139	@[simp]
   140	lemma one_val (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (1 : picEt C T).1 U = 1 :=
   141	  rfl
   142	
   143	@[simp]
   144	lemma inv_val (s : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (s⁻¹).1 U = (s.1 U)⁻¹ :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end picEt

   149	/-! ## The affine comparison -/
   150	
   151	section Affine
   152	
   153	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   154	
   155	/-- The top affine open of an affine test object. -/
   156	def overSpecTopAffine : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens :=
   157	  ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top_overSpec k A⟩
   158	
   159	/-- Evaluation at the top affine open of an affine test, composed with the
   160	`ΓSpecIso`-transport into the test algebra: the forward direction of the affine
   161	comparison. -/
   162	def picEtToAff : picEt C (overSpec k A) →* PicEtAff C A :=
   163	  (PicEtAff.congr C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A)).toMonoidHom.comp
   164	    (picEt.eval C (overSpec k A) (overSpecTopAffine A))
   165	
   166	lemma picEtToAff_apply (s : picEt C (overSpec k A)) :
   167	    picEtToAff C A s
   168	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
   169	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) :=
   170	  rfl
   171	
   172	/-- The section of `picEt` over an affine test determined by a plus class of the test
   173	algebra: restrict from the top affine open — the inverse direction of the affine
   174	comparison. -/
   175	def picEtOfAff : PicEtAff C A →* picEt C (overSpec k A) where
   176	  toFun x :=
   177	    ⟨fun U => PicEtAff.mapAlg C
   178	      ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
   179	        (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom) x,
   180	      fun U V h => by rw [← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp, ← AlgHom.comp_assoc,
   181	        Over.resAlgHom_comp]⟩
   182	  map_one' := picEt.ext fun U => map_one (PicEtAff.mapAlg C _)
   183	  map_mul' x y := picEt.ext fun U => map_mul (PicEtAff.mapAlg C _) x y
   184	
   185	lemma picEtOfAff_val (x : PicEtAff C A) (U : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens) :
   186	    (picEtOfAff C A x).1 U
   187	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C
   188	          ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
   189	            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom) x :=
   190	  rfl
   191	
   192	private lemma picEtOfAff_comp_picEtToAff :
   193	    (picEtOfAff C A).comp (picEtToAff C A) = MonoidHom.id (picEt C (overSpec k A)) := by
   194	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun s => picEt.ext fun U => ?_
   195	  calc ((picEtOfAff C A) (picEtToAff C A s)).1 U
   196	      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C
   197	          (((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
   198	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom).comp
   199	            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom)

   202	    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top)
   203	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) := by
   204	        rw [AlgHom.comp_assoc,
   205	          show (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom.comp
   206	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
   207	            = AlgHom.id k Γ((overSpec k A).left, ⊤) from
   208	            AlgHom.ext fun a => (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm_apply_apply a,
   209	          AlgHom.comp_id]

   217	          ((Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom.comp
   218	            ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
   219	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom)) x :=

   233	affine-opens limit `picEt` collapses by evaluation at the terminal element `⊤` of the

   243	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) :=

   251	          ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp

     9	/-!
    10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
    11	
    12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
    13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
    14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
    15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
    16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
    19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
    21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
    22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
    23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
    25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
    27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
    28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
    29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
    30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
    31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
    32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
    33	-/
    34	
    35	set_option autoImplicit false
    36	
    37	universe u
    38	
    39	open CategoryTheory
    40	
    41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    42	
    43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    45	
    46	noncomputable section
    47	
    48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
    49	
    50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
    51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
    52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
    53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
    54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
    56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    57	
    58	section DegAt
    59	
    60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    61	
    62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
    63	@[simp]
    64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
    65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
    66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
    67	
    68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
    69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
    71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
    72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
    73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
    74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
    75	
    76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
    77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
    79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
    80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
    81	  rfl
    82	
    83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
    84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
    85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
    86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
    87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
    89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
    90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
    91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
    92	
    93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
    94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
    97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
    98	
    99	end DegAt
   100	
   101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
   102	
   103	variable (C) in
   104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
   105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
   106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
   107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
   108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   109	    degAt lam t = 0}
   110	  one_mem' := by
   111	    intro K _ _ t
   112	    exact degAt_one t
   113	  mul_mem' := by
   114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
   115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
   116	  inv_mem' := by
   117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
   118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
   119	
   120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
   121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
   122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
   123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
   124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
   125	  Iff.rfl
   126	
   127	variable (C) in
   128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
   129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
   130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
   131	points. -/
   132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
   133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
   134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
   135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
   136	
   137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
   138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
   139	@[simp]
   140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
   141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
   142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	variable (C) in
   146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
   147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
   148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
   149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
   150	functor. -/
   151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
   152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
   153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
   154	  map_id T := by
   155	    ext lam U
   156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
   157	  map_comp g h := by
   158	    ext lam U
   159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
   160	
   161	@[simp]
   162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
   163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
   164	  rfl
   165	
   166	@[simp]
   167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
   168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
   169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
   170	  rfl
   171	
   172	variable (C) in
   173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
   174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
   175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
   176	def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
   177	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
   178	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
   179	
   180	end
   181	
   182	end AlgebraicGeometry

    59	/-- A rank-one presentation of a genus-degree plus class on an affine test.
    60	
    61	The two equality fields prevent an unrelated cocycle datum or line bundle from serving as a
    62	witness: `representative` presents the input plus class, `datum_class` presents that same
    63	relative Picard class, and `module_iso` identifies the resulting cocycle sheaf with the
    64	underlying base-ring sheaf of `module`. -/
    65	structure PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    66	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    67	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    68	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    69	  represents :
    70	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    71	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
    72	  datum_class :
    73	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
    74	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
    75	  module : (relCurve C cover.Carrier).Modules
    76	  module_iso :
    77	    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
    78	      (Over.mk (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier))) module ≅ datum.sheaf
    79	  line_bundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle module
    80	  native_pushforward_base_change :
    81	    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    82	      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    83	      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
    84	      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    85	        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
    86	      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app module)
    87	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
    88	  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    89	  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    90	  h0_rank_one :
    91	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
    92	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1

   106	This is derived from `P.h1_vanishing`; it is not an independently chosen witness. -/
   107	noncomputable def h0BaseChange (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   108	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   109	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :

   111	      Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0 :=

   115	/-- The canonical evaluation map attached to a tied local rank-one presentation. -/
   116	noncomputable def evaluation (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :
   117	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
   118	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj
   119	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   120	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ⟶
   121	      P.module :=

   123	    (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).counit.app P.module

   127	/-- The canonical native pushforward base-change isomorphism supplied by the presentation.
   128	
   129	The isomorphism is not chosen independently: its hom is definitionally
   130	`(canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.module`. -/
   131	noncomputable def nativeBaseChangeIso (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   132	    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
   133	    (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
   134	    (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)
   135	    (sq : IsPullback g' f'
   136	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) g) :
   137	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj
   138	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   139	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅
   140	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f').obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj P.module) := by
   141	  exact @asIso _ _ _ _ ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.module)

   145	noncomputable def nativeBaseChangeIsoAffine (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   146	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   147	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
   148	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
   149	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.cover.Carrier B)))).obj
   150	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   151	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅

events.text: The existing rank-one predicate is presentation-level: membership requires a `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` on every affine pullback, while the Riemann–Roch side already exposes the positive-twist and exact point-drop lemmas. I’m now checking the exact translation and presentation bridges so the new theorem has the consumer’s literal type rather than a parallel numerical surrogate.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOnePresentation
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Image

/-!
# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map

`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.

The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not prove that
`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme, and it reserves `DivRankOneOpen` for the
future actual open subscheme of the divisor representer.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

noncomputable section

/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.

Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
def PicRankOneOpen :
    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
      apply Subtype.ext
      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    rw [e]
    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)

/-- The inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` under the affine widened Abel transformation.

This name deliberately records only a presentation-theoretic preimage.  It is not the future
open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/
def divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff :
    Subfunctor (divFunctorAff C (genus C)) :=
  (PicRankOneOpen pi).preimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))

/-- The same presentation preimage on the Yoneda functor of the canonical genus divisor
representer. -/
def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).preimage
    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom

/-- The affine Abel transformation restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
def rankOneAbelAff :
    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor ⟶
      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))

/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom

/-- The represented genus Abel map restricted to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
def rankOneAbelRepresented :
    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModulesBaseSheaf
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModulesPushforwardBaseChange
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafH0BaseChange
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.LocalGenerators
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjectiveH0BaseChange
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjectiveSite
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0EndgameContract
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RingDatumEngine
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisorsClass

/-!
# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus

An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
test and ties every piece of data to the input class:

* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.

No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
  CartesianMonoidalCategory

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

/-- A rank-one presentation of a genus-degree plus class on an affine test.

The two equality fields prevent an unrelated cocycle datum or line bundle from serving as a
witness: `representative` presents the input plus class, `datum_class` presents that same
relative Picard class, and `module_iso` identifies the resulting cocycle sheaf with the
underlying base-ring sheaf of `module`. -/
structure PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
  representative : descentClasses C cover
  represents :
    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
  datum_class :
    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
  module : (relCurve C cover.Carrier).Modules
  module_iso :
    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
      (Over.mk (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier))) module ≅ datum.sheaf
  line_bundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle module
  native_pushforward_base_change :
    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app module)
  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
  h0_rank_one :
    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1

namespace PicRankOneLocalPresentation

variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}

noncomputable local instance presentationModuleSections
    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) (U : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens) :
    Module P.cover.Carrier Γ(P.module, U) :=
  Scheme.moduleKSections
    (Over.mk (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))) P.module U

/-- The canonical `H^0` base-change equivalence attached to a rank-one presentation.

This is derived from `P.h1_vanishing`; it is not an independently chosen witness. -/
noncomputable def h0BaseChange (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
    B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] (Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) ≃ₗ[B]
      Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0 :=
  P.datum.datumH0BaseChange B
    ((subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff P.datum).mpr P.h1_vanishing)

/-- The canonical evaluation map attached to a tied local rank-one presentation. -/
noncomputable def evaluation (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ⟶
      P.module :=
  (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
    (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).counit.app P.module

/-! ## Native pushforward base change and evaluation coherence -/

/-- The canonical native pushforward base-change isomorphism supplied by the presentation.

The isomorphism is not chosen independently: its hom is definitionally
`(canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.module`. -/
noncomputable def nativeBaseChangeIso (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)

**Title corrected (issue I-0615): this file is steps 4 and 5, not "4–6".**  Step 6 — feeding the
drop's output `Σ` back as the chart index — is NOT here and is not discharged anywhere; see the
DEFECT section of `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageTest.lean`, which explains why the drop stage and the
index stage carry different `Z`.  The original "4–6" wording is what that retraction corrects.

`w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–5 happen entirely on the curve over the splitting field `L`.  This file
runs them and hands the result to `Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean`'s introduction rule, so
that what comes out is membership of `chartLocus`.

## The statement, and what is a hypothesis rather than a construction

`exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop` takes:

* the presentation of the *twisted* fibre class over `L` by a Čech class `M`
  (`hM` — supplied at step 1 by `picEtAffineEquiv_map_chartTwistFactor_eq_unit`);
* a divisor `W₀` in that class with vanishing `H¹` and degree `g + e`
  (`hdeg`/`h1` — supplied at step 4: the class's degree is computed by
  `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegree.lean`, and the vanishing comes from the fibre's OWN
  vanishing bound, which is where step 3's per-fibre `m` is spent);
* the admissible point oracle at `L` (`hdense`/`hPcl`/`hPdeg` — supplied at step 5 by
  `Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`'s density keystone at the base-changed `K_s`-points).

and produces an `S ≥ 0` of degree `e`, supported in the oracle, with `h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`,
`h¹ = 0`, together with `IsSplitWitness` at the twisted class.

**What is deliberately a hypothesis:** the *existence* of `W₀` of the right degree with
`h¹ = 0`.  That is DAT-0a at the fibre field, and per `w4-datb` §0.2.2 (the I-0204 discipline)
its bound `b_L` is a **per-fibre** constant that provably does not transport from `k` — so it
must be chosen at `L`, inside the coverage proof, against `L`'s own instance.  Threading it as
a hypothesis here keeps that choice visible instead of burying it: a caller who cannot produce
`W₀` has not yet done step 3.

**Why the `h⁰ = 1` conclusion is carried even though `IsSplitWitness` does not ask for it:**
the witness predicate asks only for vanishing `H¹` (documented at `IsSplitWitness`; the
worksheets' "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`" is stronger than what the tree's
predicates state).  But `h⁰ = 1` is what DAT-C's normalization and GAP-2's uniqueness need, and
it is free here — the drop produces it.  Dropping it from the conclusion would force a later
lane to re-run the induction.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop` — **the fibre step of B-5**: the greedy drop
  at `L`, packaged as `IsSplitWitness` of the twisted class plus the `h⁰ = 1` normalization.

/-! ## The fibre step -/

variable (C) in
/-- **B-5's fibre step** (`w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–5, run at the splitting field; **not** step 6 —
see the header correction and issue I-0615).

Given the twisted fibre class presented over `L` by `M`, a divisor `W₀` in `M` of degree
`g + e` with vanishing `H¹`, and an admissible point oracle `P` on the `L`-curve, the greedy
drop produces `S` of degree `e` supported in `P` with `h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1` and `h¹(W₀ − S) = 0`;
and the class of `W₀` itself already certifies `IsSplitWitness` of the twisted class.

The two conclusions serve different consumers, which is why both are returned: the
`IsSplitWitness` half is `chartLocus` membership (`w4-datb` §1.2's target), while the

theorem exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
    [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
    (g e : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    (W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀
      = M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (g : ℤ) + e)
    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1))
    (P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
    (hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
      (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1) :
    IsSplitWitness C (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C m Z) (overSpec k K))
      ∧ ∃ S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (e : ℤ) ∧
        (∀ (x : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
          (hx : x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)),
          coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
        Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) = 1 ∧
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
          ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) 1) := by
  refine ⟨isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1, ?_⟩
  -- the χ-value at the fibre field, transported from `k` (genus is base-field invariant)
  -- The instance pack of `BaseChangeInstances` is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling
  -- `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`, not to the `relCurve` alias, so `chi_relCurve_baseField`'s
  -- `relCurve`-spelled binders do not synthesise without these three re-keyings.
  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
  have hχL : Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (g : ℤ) :=
    chi_relCurve_baseField C L g hχ
  exact exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one (K := L) g hχL P hdense hPcl hPdeg W₀ e hdeg h1

end

/-!
# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
index per point of `T`".

**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
connection is what this file supplies.

## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline

Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:

* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
  strengthening chosen to be provable.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content

Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
statement is what made it look gated. -/

/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**

If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
Zariski covering sieve of `T`.

The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.

Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)

/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/

variable (C) in
/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.

The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
it, and every point `t` of `T`:

* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.

Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.

**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
  intro T s
  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩

variable (C) in
/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.

The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)

/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening

A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/

variable (C) in
/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**

The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.

**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
